chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The most superior of worship is the habitual contemplation in Allah and in His power.
ai.seo_question: What is considered the best form of worship according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) identifies the continuous contemplation (tafakkur) of Allah and His power as the supreme act of worship, elevating intellectual reflection to the status of ritual devotion. In Shia scholarly tradition, this hadith underscores that true worship is not merely mechanical but rooted in deep cognitive awareness of the Divine, a concept central to the epistemological foundations of Usul al-Din. This emphasis on 'idman' (habitual continuity) suggests that sustained mental engagement with God's attributes is more meritorious than sporadic, intense acts of physical worship.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from one of his men,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The most superior of the worship is being habitual in ‘التَّفَكُّرِ’ the contemplation regarding Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and regarding His<sup>azwj</sup> Ordainment’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from certain individuals of his people from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
The most virtuous form of worship is thinking about Allah very often and about His power. ’”
